topic: EU AI Act Compliance for Developers: August 2026 Deadline Guide

key_points: Focus on enterprise deploying high-risk AI
SME vs. large enterprise compliance paths
Impact on dev teams using AI coding assistants
How to classify AI tools used in development

stats.fact: EU AI Act fully applicable on 2 August 2026, covering high-risk AI systems, transparency rules (Article 50), and innovation measures
Prohibited AI practices fines: up to €35 million or 7% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher
High-risk AI system non-compliance fines: up to €15 million or 3% of total worldwide annual turnover
Incorrect or misleading information penalties: up to €7.5 million or 1.5% of annual turnover
SME compliance costs typically range from €50,000 to €500,000 depending on use case complexity
Large enterprises (>€1B revenue) face $8–15 million initial investment for high-risk AI systems
GPAI models with ≥10²⁵ training FLOPs are presumed to have systemic risk and face stricter obligations
Technical documentation and post-market monitoring records must be retained for 10 years
Automatic logging for high-risk AI systems must retain logs for at least 6 months
High-risk AI non-compliance expected to account for over 70% of enforcement actions post-2026
AI Omnibus political agreement reached May 7, 2026, extending Annex III standalone high-risk AI deadline to December 2, 2027
Prohibited practices and GPAI model rules already enforceable as of February and August 2025 respectively

angles: The AI Omnibus May 2026 deal is a game-changer: Annex III standalone high-risk systems now have until December 2027 — clarify what August 2026 still covers vs. what got extended
Developer-specific compliance gaps: most guides target compliance officers, not engineers — focus on what dev teams must actually build (logging, human oversight UI, documentation APIs)
GPAI open-source trap: developers releasing open-source models get partial exemptions, but NOT if systemic risk threshold (10²⁵ FLOPs) is crossed — critical nuance
AI-generated code risk: using AI coding assistants to build regulated systems creates compliance liability for the human developer/deployer — unexplored angle
Cost reality check: €50K–€500K for SMEs vs. $8–15M for enterprises — provide concrete breakdown by system type to help developers budget compliance
Conformity assessment is self-assessment for most Annex III systems: no third-party body needed unless Annex I product-safety rules apply — simplifies the path
August 2026 transparency deadline still applies: chatbots, deepfakes, emotion recognition disclosure requirements kick in on August 2 regardless of Omnibus delay
